108	   you want is not documented, it does not exist — use the documented one, or

113	   `Button view`, `Icon data`. Per-component traps live in the package's own
114	   `dist/docs`.

117	   (typically `tsc --noEmit`; for monorepos, the workspace's typecheck script).
118	   Fix every error before reporting completion — a type error almost always
119	   means a wrong/invented prop, a wrong import path, or a version mismatch,
120	   which is precisely what Steps 0–1 were meant to prevent.

124	     docs snapshot — the docs may be from a different minor. Re-ground: read
125	     the package's `dist/docs/INDEX.md` in `node_modules` for the exact
126	     installed types.
127	   - If the typecheck is unavailable (no TS in the project), say so
128	     explicitly and ask the user how they want to verify; do not silently
129	     skip verification.
130	   - **Escape hatch.** If the user explicitly waived verification ("just
131	     sketch it", "quick prototype", "no need to check"), you may skip the
132	     typecheck — but state this plainly in your reply: *"typecheck skipped by
133	     user request — code is not verified"*. Do not skip silently.
134	   - **Know what typecheck does not cover.** A green `tsc` proves the API is
135	     real; it says nothing about layout or contrast. Before reporting done,
136	     say so, and either check or list for the user to check by hand: the
137	     screen in both `light` and `dark` themes (text and controls on colored
138	     fills especially), narrow (~375px) and wide (~1400px) viewports for
139	     horizontal overflow, and empty / loading / error states.
140	
141	## Hard rules
142	
143	- **`@gravity-ui/uikit` MUST be installed in every Gravity UI project.** It is
144	  the base component + design-token library every other `@gravity-ui/*` package
145	  builds on; without it components render unstyled. If `package.json` lacks it,
146	  stop and have the user install and configure it first (setup:
147	  `https://gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/llms.txt`).
148	- **Read `package.json` before importing any `@gravity-ui/*` package.** Never
149	  assume a package is installed; never assume its major version.
150	- **Do not invent props or components.** Before using a component API you are
151	  not 100% sure of, check `rules/hallucination-traps.md` (ecosystem patterns)
152	  and the component's README in `dist/docs`. If still unsure, ask the user
153	  rather than guessing.
154	- **Never guess icon names** — they are hallucinated more often than not. To
155	  match an icon from a screenshot/photo/mock, run `scripts/icon-image-search.sh`
156	  (reverse image search). With only a description, look the name up on
157	  `gravity-ui.com/icons` or ask the user — do not invent one. Then pass it as an
158	  object (`<Icon data={CheckIcon} />`), never a string key. See
159	  `references/icons.md`.
160	- **Theming uses semantic `--g-*` tokens.** Never hardcode colors (`#fff`,
161	  `blue-500`); never hand-write `dark:` overrides. Full token tables live in
162	  `references/theming.md`; the cross-cutting traps (partial brand overrides,
163	  a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, controls on a brand background) live in
164	  `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
165	- **Required setup is package-specific** (style imports, `ThemeProvider`,
166	  peer-deps). It lives in each package's root README under "Required setup" —
167	  read it once per package, do not rely on memory.
168	
169	## What NOT to do
170	
171	These are the five most common ways agents break Gravity UI code. They are
172	already implied by the rules above; this section exists as an explicit
173	stop-sign. If you are about to do any of these, stop and re-ground.
174	
175	- **Do not substitute non-Gravity libraries.** No MUI, Ant Design, plain
176	  `<input>`/`<button>`, or look-alike component libs. Use the `@gravity-ui/*`
177	  package the task needs.
178	- **Do not invent component APIs or props.** If a prop is not in the docs you
179	  read in Step 1, it does not exist — do not write `variant=`, `color=`,
180	  `name=` (on `Icon`), or a `header-3` variant. Use the documented prop or
181	  ask the user. See `rules/hallucination-traps.md`.
182	- **Do not use the `/llms/<pkg>/llms.txt` "latest" alias as a fallback.** It
183	  serves the newest major, which may differ from the installed one and have a
184	  different API. The versioned online fallback is the major-line URL
185	  (`/llms/<pkg>/<major>/llms.txt`); below that, go LOCAL.
186	- **Do not partial-brand.** Setting only `--g-color-base-brand` leaves
187	  selection, focus, links and contrast on the default accent — a mismatched
188	  UI. Override the full brand token set, on each theme you support.
189	- **Do not override internal markup with `[class*='…']` / ID selectors.**
190	  That's written against one DOM structure and breaks silently when the
191	  component changes. Climb the customization ladder
192	  (global token → component CSS API → narrow flagged hack) before ever
193	  touching structure.
194	
195	## Deeper material — read on demand
196	
197	These files live alongside this SKILL.md and load only when relevant:
198	
199	- `references/package-routing.md` — offline snapshot of the ecosystem catalog
200	  (`gravity-ui.com/llms.txt`), refreshed each skill release. Used as the
201	  offline fallback in Step 0.
202	- `references/theming.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/theming.md`:
203	  `--g-*` token layers, `ThemeProvider`, branding, custom themes, scoped
204	  themes, `uikit-themer`. The bundled copy may lag — read
205	  `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/theming.md` for the
206	  version-matched file.
207	- `references/layout.md` — verbatim copy of uikit's `docs/layout.md`:
208	  spacing scale (`--g-spacing-*`), `Flex`/`Box`, `Row`/`Col`/`Container`
209	  grid, breakpoints, `useLayoutContext`.
210	- `references/icons.md` — finding an icon by image
211	  (`scripts/icon-image-search.sh`) or on gravity-ui.com/icons; the
212	  object-vs-string rendering rule.
213	- `rules/hallucination-traps.md` — Incorrect/Correct pairs for the most
214	  commonly invented APIs: typography variants (`header-3..6` don't exist, no
215	  `Heading`), the flex contract (`min-width:0`, who shrinks), theming traps
216	  (partial brand overrides, a `ThemeProvider` that themes the whole page, customization
217	  ladder), `Button view` not `variant`, `Icon data` not `name`. Per-component
218	  traps live in each package's `dist/docs`, not here.

20	# Theming, Colors & Branding
21	
22	[English](theming.md) | [Русский](theming-ru.md)
23	
24	We use and recommend CSS variables for theming.
25	
26	Everything is driven by CSS custom properties prefixed with `--g-*`. There is no runtime styling API you need to call — you set variables and components pick them up.
27	
28	```tsx
29	import {ThemeProvider, Button} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
30	import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/fonts.css';
31	import '@gravity-ui/uikit/styles/styles.css';
32	
33	export const App = () => (
34	  <ThemeProvider theme="system">
35	    <Button view="action">Branded button</Button>
36	  </ThemeProvider>
37	);
38	```
39	
40	## How theming works
41	
42	All variables live on the root class `.g-root`, which `ThemeProvider` assigns to `<body>` by
43	default (change the target with the `scoped` prop). Color variables additionally live on a
44	per-theme class `.g-root_theme_{themeName}`, so switching the theme swaps one set of values for
45	another.
46	
47	```
48	.g-root                      → structural tokens (spacing, typography metrics, border radius)
49	.g-root_theme_light          → color tokens for the light theme
50	.g-root_theme_dark           → color tokens for the dark theme
51	```
52	
53	To customize anything, you provide new values for these CSS variables — for a single theme, for
54	several themes, or globally. If you support more than one theme, set color overrides **per theme**.
55	
56	## Themes
57	
58	UIKit ships 4 built-in themes:
59	
60	| Theme      | Description                          |
61	| ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
62	| `light`    | Default light theme                  |
63	| `dark`     | Default dark theme                   |
64	| `light-hc` | Light, high-contrast (accessibility) |

20	# Layout components and spacings
21	
22	This guide covers UIKit's layout foundations: a shared **spacing** scale (`--g-spacing-*`, used
23	everywhere via tokens and props) and a responsive **grid** (`Container`/`Row`/`Col`), plus the
24	flexbox-based `Flex`/`Box` primitives built on top of them. Compose pages from these instead of
25	raw `div`s and inline styles.
26	
27	## Spacing
28	
29	Spacing in UIKit is a **scale**, not free-form pixels. You reference a step (`1`, `2`, … `10`)
30	and the design system turns it into a concrete size. Sticking to the scale is what keeps rhythm
31	consistent across the whole app, and lets you rescale everything from a single variable.
32	
33	### The scale
34	
35	Every step is a multiple of a base unit (`--g-spacing-base`, `4px` by default), so `step × 4px`:
36	
37	| Step  | CSS variable       | Size |
38	| ----- | ------------------ | ---- |
39	| `0`   | `--g-spacing-0`    | 0    |
40	| `0.5` | `--g-spacing-half` | 2px  |
41	| `1`   | `--g-spacing-1`    | 4px  |
42	| `2`   | `--g-spacing-2`    | 8px  |
43	| `3`   | `--g-spacing-3`    | 12px |
44	| `4`   | `--g-spacing-4`    | 16px |
45	| `5`   | `--g-spacing-5`    | 20px |
46	| `6`   | `--g-spacing-6`    | 24px |
47	| `7`   | `--g-spacing-7`    | 28px |
48	| `8`   | `--g-spacing-8`    | 32px |
49	| `9`   | `--g-spacing-9`    | 36px |
50	| `10`  | `--g-spacing-10`   | 40px |
51	
52	Because every step is derived from `--g-spacing-base`, changing that one value rescales the
53	entire spacing system proportionally (see [Customization](#customization)).
54	
55	### Ways to apply spacing
56	
57	There are three ways to consume the scale — pick by context:
58	
59	**1. Component props** — spacing **between** children of `Flex`/`Box`, via the `gap` prop:
60	
61	```tsx
62	import {Flex} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
63	
64	<Flex gap={5}>
65	  <Button />
66	  <Button />
67	</Flex>; // 20px between children
68	```
69	
70	**2. CSS custom properties** — the same steps as `--g-spacing-{step}` variables, for use in your
71	own styles (e.g. `--g-spacing-half` for the `0.5` step):
72	
73	```css
74	.example-class {
75	  margin-right: var(--g-spacing-5); /* 20px */
76	  padding: var(--g-spacing-2) var(--g-spacing-4);
77	}
78	```
79	
80	**3. The `spacing()` utility** — for one-off margins/paddings on any element without hand-writing
81	class names. It returns a generated class name string:
82	
83	```tsx
84	import {spacing} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
85	
86	<>
87	  <Button className={spacing({mr: 5})}>button 1</Button>
88	  <Button className={spacing({mt: 2, px: 4})}>button 2</Button>
89	</>;
90	```
91	
92	`sp` is a shorter alias: `import {sp} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'` → `sp({mr: 5})`.
93	
94	Supported keys (each takes a scale step):
95	
96	| Key                 | Property                          |
97	| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
98	| `m`                 | `margin`                          |
99	| `mt` `mr` `mb` `ml` | `margin-top/right/bottom/left`    |
100	| `mx`                | horizontal margin (left + right)  |
101	| `my`                | vertical margin (top + bottom)    |
102	| `p`                 | `padding`                         |
103	| `pt` `pr` `pb` `pl` | `padding-top/right/bottom/left`   |
104	| `px`                | horizontal padding (left + right) |
105	| `py`                | vertical padding (top + bottom)   |
106	
107	You can pass a second argument to merge extra class names: `spacing({mr: 5}, myClassName)`.
108	
109	> **Rule of thumb:** `gap` for spacing between siblings in a `Flex`/`Box`; the `spacing()`/`sp()`
110	> utility for one-off offsets on an element; raw `--g-spacing-*` variables inside your own CSS.
111	> Always use scale steps, never hard-coded pixels.
112	
113	### Customization
114	
115	Override the base unit to rescale the whole system. Do it via CSS at the project level:
116	
117	```css
118	:root {
119	  --g-spacing-base: 5px; /* now step 5 = 25px, etc. */
120	}
121	```
122	
123	Or through the layout theme, which keeps the JS `Space` values and CSS variables in sync:
124	
125	```tsx
126	import {ThemeProvider, LayoutTheme} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
127	
128	const config: LayoutTheme = {
129	    spaceBaseSize: 5,
130	};
131	
132	export const App = () => {
133	    return (
134	        <ThemeProvider layout={{config, fixBreakpoints: true}}>
135	            {...}
136	        </ThemeProvider>
137	    );
138	};
139	```
140	
141	## Screen sizes:
142	
143	We use **mobile-first** approach. It means that you should adapt your app for desktop after completing development of mobile version.
144	The default breakpoints are:
145	
146	- `xs` - < 576px
147	- `s` - ≥ 576px;
148	- `m` - ≥ 768px;
149	- `l` - ≥ 1080px;
150	- `xl` - ≥ 1200px;
151	- `xxl` - ≥ 1400px;
152	- `xxxl` - ≥ 1920px;
153	
154	To override a breakpoint use the `breakpoints` property in the layout config:
155	
156	```tsx
157	const APP_LAYOUT_THEME: LayoutTheme = {
158	    spaceBaseSize: 4,
159	    components: {
160	        container: {
161	            gutters: 3,
162	            media: {
163	                l: {
164	                    gutters: 5,
165	                },
166	            },
167	        },
168	    },
169	    breakpoints: {
170	        s: 320,
171	        l: 980,
172	    },
173	};
174	
175	<ThemeProvider layout={{config: APP_LAYOUT_THEME}}>
176	    {...}
177	</ThemeProvider>;
178	```
179	
180	## Box
181	
182	The `Box` component is a developer friend and basic block to build other components. Aware about spacing, its own sizes and most commonly used CSS properties.
183	
184	Use it to declaratively describe elements with a fixed height/width. It also has built-in support for the most commonly used properties, such as `overflow`.
185	It is mainly used as a base unit for other components such as `Flex` and `Card`.
186	
187	It is also well suited for use as a base for data loading containers, for example:
188	
189	```tsx
190	import React, {Suspense} from 'react';
191	import {Flex, Loader} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
192

1	# Layout — spacing scale, `Flex`/`Box`, grid (`Row`/`Col`/`Container`)
2	
3	> **Source of truth:** this is a verbatim copy of
4	> [`@gravity-ui/uikit`'s `docs/layout.md`](https://github.com/gravity-ui/uikit/blob/main/docs/layout.md).
5	> The current version in the installed `node_modules` may differ — for the exact
6	> file matching your version, read
7	> `node_modules/@gravity-ui/uikit/build/docs/guides/layout.md` (or fetch the
8	> version-pinned copy at `gravity-ui.com/llms/uikit/<major>/llms.txt`).
9	>
10	> This copy is bundled offline. If a token or prop you need is missing or looks
11	> different here, prefer the version-matched source over this snapshot.
12	
13	This reference covers the **spacing scale, layout components, and responsive
14	breakpoints**. For the **flex-contract traps** — who shrinks vs who holds, why
15	`min-width:0` matters, scroll-vs-page — see
16	[`../rules/hallucination-traps.md`](../rules/hallucination-traps.md).
17	
18	---
19	
20	# Layout components and spacings
21	
22	This guide covers UIKit's layout foundations: a shared **spacing** scale (`--g-spacing-*`, used
23	everywhere via tokens and props) and a responsive **grid** (`Container`/`Row`/`Col`), plus the
24	flexbox-based `Flex`/`Box` primitives built on top of them. Compose pages from these instead of
25	raw `div`s and inline styles.
26	
27	## Spacing
28	
29	Spacing in UIKit is a **scale**, not free-form pixels. You reference a step (`1`, `2`, … `10`)
30	and the design system turns it into a concrete size. Sticking to the scale is what keeps rhythm
31	consistent across the whole app, and lets you rescale everything from a single variable.
32	
33	### The scale
34	
35	Every step is a multiple of a base unit (`--g-spacing-base`, `4px` by default), so `step × 4px`:
36	
37	| Step  | CSS variable       | Size |
38	| ----- | ------------------ | ---- |
39	| `0`   | `--g-spacing-0`    | 0    |
40	| `0.5` | `--g-spacing-half` | 2px  |
41	| `1`   | `--g-spacing-1`    | 4px  |
42	| `2`   | `--g-spacing-2`    | 8px  |
43	| `3`   | `--g-spacing-3`    | 12px |
44	| `4`   | `--g-spacing-4`    | 16px |
45	| `5`   | `--g-spacing-5`    | 20px |
46	| `6`   | `--g-spacing-6`    | 24px |
47	| `7`   | `--g-spacing-7`    | 28px |
48	| `8`   | `--g-spacing-8`    | 32px |
49	| `9`   | `--g-spacing-9`    | 36px |
50	| `10`  | `--g-spacing-10`   | 40px |
51	
52	Because every step is derived from `--g-spacing-base`, changing that one value rescales the
53	entire spacing system proportionally (see [Customization](#customization)).
54	
55	### Ways to apply spacing
56	
57	There are three ways to consume the scale — pick by context:
58	
59	**1. Component props** — spacing **between** children of `Flex`/`Box`, via the `gap` prop:
60	
61	```tsx
62	import {Flex} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
63	
64	<Flex gap={5}>
65	  <Button />
66	  <Button />
67	</Flex>; // 20px between children
68	```
69	
70	**2. CSS custom properties** — the same steps as `--g-spacing-{step}` variables, for use in your
71	own styles (e.g. `--g-spacing-half` for the `0.5` step):
72	
73	```css
74	.example-class {
75	  margin-right: var(--g-spacing-5); /* 20px */
76	  padding: var(--g-spacing-2) var(--g-spacing-4);
77	}
78	```
79	
80	**3. The `spacing()` utility** — for one-off margins/paddings on any element without hand-writing
81	class names. It returns a generated class name string:
82	
83	```tsx
84	import {spacing} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
85	
86	<>
87	  <Button className={spacing({mr: 5})}>button 1</Button>
88	  <Button className={spacing({mt: 2, px: 4})}>button 2</Button>
89	</>;
90	```
91	
92	`sp` is a shorter alias: `import {sp} from '@gravity-ui/uikit'` → `sp({mr: 5})`.
93	
94	Supported keys (each takes a scale step):
95	
96	| Key                 | Property                          |
97	| ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
98	| `m`                 | `margin`                          |
99	| `mt` `mr` `mb` `ml` | `margin-top/right/bottom/left`    |
100	| `mx`                | horizontal margin (left + right)  |
101	| `my`                | vertical margin (top + bottom)    |
102	| `p`                 | `padding`                         |
103	| `pt` `pr` `pb` `pl` | `padding-top/right/bottom/left`   |
104	| `px`                | horizontal padding (left + right) |
105	| `py`                | vertical padding (top + bottom)   |
106	
107	You can pass a second argument to merge extra class names: `spacing({mr: 5}, myClassName)`.
108	
109	> **Rule of thumb:** `gap` for spacing between siblings in a `Flex`/`Box`; the `spacing()`/`sp()`
110	> utility for one-off offsets on an element; raw `--g-spacing-*` variables inside your own CSS.
111	> Always use scale steps, never hard-coded pixels.
112	
113	### Customization
114	
115	Override the base unit to rescale the whole system. Do it via CSS at the project level:
116	
117	```css
118	:root {
119	  --g-spacing-base: 5px; /* now step 5 = 25px, etc. */
120	}
121	```
122	
123	Or through the layout theme, which keeps the JS `Space` values and CSS variables in sync:
124	
125	```tsx
126	import {ThemeProvider, LayoutTheme} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
127	
128	const config: LayoutTheme = {
129	    spaceBaseSize: 5,
130	};
131	
132	export const App = () => {
133	    return (
134	        <ThemeProvider layout={{config, fixBreakpoints: true}}>
135	            {...}
136	        </ThemeProvider>
137	    );
138	};
139	```
140	
141	## Screen sizes:
142	
143	We use **mobile-first** approach. It means that you should adapt your app for desktop after completing development of mobile version.
144	The default breakpoints are:
145	
146	- `xs` - < 576px
147	- `s` - ≥ 576px;
148	- `m` - ≥ 768px;
149	- `l` - ≥ 1080px;
150	- `xl` - ≥ 1200px;
151	- `xxl` - ≥ 1400px;
152	- `xxxl` - ≥ 1920px;
153	
154	To override a breakpoint use the `breakpoints` property in the layout config:
155	
156	```tsx
157	const APP_LAYOUT_THEME: LayoutTheme = {
158	    spaceBaseSize: 4,
159	    components: {
160	        container: {
161	            gutters: 3,
162	            media: {
163	                l: {
164	                    gutters: 5,
165	                },
166	            },
167	        },
168	    },
169	    breakpoints: {
170	        s: 320,
171	        l: 980,
172	    },
173	};
174	
175	<ThemeProvider layout={{config: APP_LAYOUT_THEME}}>
176	    {...}
177	</ThemeProvider>;
178	```
179	
180	## Box
181	
182	The `Box` component is a developer friend and basic block to build other components. Aware about spacing, its own sizes and most commonly used CSS properties.
183	
184	Use it to declaratively describe elements with a fixed height/width. It also has built-in support for the most commonly used properties, such as `overflow`.
185	It is mainly used as a base unit for other components such as `Flex` and `Card`.
186	
187	It is also well suited for use as a base for data loading containers, for example:
188	
189	```tsx
190	import React, {Suspense} from 'react';
191	import {Flex, Loader} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
192	
193	// `Flex` extended from `Box` component and enriched flexbox model properties
194	<Flex centerContent width="100%" height="100%">
195	  <Suspense fallback={<Loader size="m" />}>
196	    <LazyLoadedComponent />
197	  </Suspense>
198	</Flex>;
199	```

Приложение готово: три страницы с боковой навигацией и переключателем светлой и тёмной темы. `npm run build` (проверка типов и сборка) проходит без ошибок. В браузере я приложение не запускал, визуально его не проверял.

**Что внутри**
- **Страницы:** «Главная», «Задачи» (добавление, отметка выполнено, удаление) и «Настройки» (показывает текущую тему).
- **Навигация:** `AsideHeader` из `@gravity-ui/navigation`. Адрес меняется на `#/home`, `#/tasks`, `#/settings`, поэтому страницы открываются по прямой ссылке и работает кнопка «назад».
- **Тема:** переключатель «Тёмная тема» в шапке страницы. Выбор сохраняется в localStorage. Список задач тоже хранится там и не теряется при переходах.

**Решения, которые стоит проверить**
- **Версия navigation.** Последняя версия (8.0.0) требует uikit 8, а в проекте закреплён uikit 7.43.0. Я поставил `@gravity-ui/navigation@7.1.3`, которая работает с uikit 7 (peer `^7.42.0`). Uikit не обновлял.
- **`@bem-react/classname`.** Это peer-зависимость navigation, поэтому я её тоже поставил. Из-за `--save-exact` она попала в `dependencies` с точной версией 1.8.0.
- **`ThemeProvider` перенесён.** Раньше он был в `main.tsx` со статичной темой. Теперь он в `App.tsx`, потому что тема управляется переключателем. CSS-импорты остались в `main.tsx`.
- **Роутинг без библиотеки.** Использовал hash-роутинг без `react-router`, чтобы не добавлять зависимость.

**Не проверено**
- Внешний вид в светлой и тёмной теме, на узком (~375px) и широком (~1400px) экране, пустой список задач. Это надо посмотреть вручную: `npm run dev`.
- При установке npm сообщил о 5 уязвимостях в зависимостях. Я их не разбирал и `npm audit fix --force` не запускал.

Новые файлы: `src/router.ts`, `src/theme.ts`, `src/pages/`. Изменены `src/App.tsx`, `src/main.tsx` и `package.json`.
